outcome: Add the repository fields to package.json and a GitHub Releases to npm publish workflow modelled on DriftSeal's
criteria: package.json carries repository, homepage, and bugs pointing at github.com/rowan-hiro/inkan
A workflow publishes to npm with OIDC trusted publishing when a GitHub Release is published, runs the tests first, and mirrors DriftSeal's structure with Inkan's name and Node 22
A CI workflow runs the tests on push and pull request, if DriftSeal has one; otherwise this criterion is withdrawn by amend with the reason
README states how a release is cut, and the one-time npm trusted publisher setup the person must do is written down rather than assumed

note: package.json gained homepage, bugs, and repository for github.com/rowan-hiro/inkan plus a test:package script. .github/workflows/test.yml mirrors DriftSeal's: push to main and pull requests, Node 22.x/24.x/26.x, static checks, tests, the history benchmark, and a package smoke on ubuntu, macos, and windows; no install step because there are no dependencies and no lockfile. .github/workflows/publish.yml mirrors DriftSeal's OIDC publish on GitHub Release with the tag-equals-version check, tests, package smoke, and npm publish --access public. scripts/test-package.mjs packs, installs, and drives the installed CLI through init, begin, end, check, and log; it passes locally. README gained a Releasing section that names the one-time trusted-publisher setup on npmjs.com and the by-hand fallback for a first publish, since the npm docs do not say whether a never-published package can take a trusted publisher. CI itself has not run yet at close; the push after this commit is its first run.
